author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Top tennis players are moving their campaign for greater influence and improved financial terms into a new Player Advisory Council that will negotiate with the four Grand Slam tournaments, Reuters reported Monday.

The campaign began in 2025 with demands for a stronger player voice in Grand Slam decision-making, increased welfare funding and a proposal for players to receive 22% of tournament revenues as prize money by 2030.

Players increased pressure this year by cutting short media obligations at the French Open and Wimbledon. The tournaments responded with larger prize pools, including a record $108 million at the U.S. Open, according to Reuters.

The group said the new council will allow players to work directly with tournament organizers on an ongoing basis. The U.S. Open has also committed $2 million toward player welfare, a move the players welcomed while saying more goals remain unresolved.

Players said they reserve the right to restart public action if the council does not produce meaningful progress. For now, the new structure shifts the dispute from tournament-week protests toward formal negotiations.
dek: Players seeking a greater role in tournament decisions and a larger share of revenues will pursue negotiations through a new council.
headline: Tennis players move pay campaign into new Grand Slam advisory council
